mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate above 4% over the prior month reduces the discount rate applied to future earnings expectations, lowering the present value of expected corporate profits and thereby depressing S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises by more than 0.25% in a month
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are positive in >70% of similar rising-rate periods, or the 20-day discount rate premium (differential between 20-day forward and spot log returns) turns negative.

mechanism_narrative: When unemployment falls below 5% for two consecutive months, increased labor market participation and reduced worker displacement expectations boost consumer confidence, driving S&P 500 forward returns positively over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE falls below 5% for two consecutive months
failure_condition: In regimes meeting the trigger, 20-day forward returns are not statistically higher than during comparable tight-labor periods (p > 0.05), or the 60-day unemployment duration remains above 4.5 months.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in personal consumption expenditures (PCE) relative to GDP (PCEPCE-GDP) exceeding 2 percentage points in a month indicates excess demand, which accelerates corporate investment plans and elevates S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 days.
candidate_trigger: PCEPCE-GDP growth rate > 2% in a month
failure_condition: In >80% of similar demand-driven months, the 5-day forward return is not statistically positive (p > 0.1), or the PCEPCE-GDP growth rate does not precede the return by at least 1 day in the walk-forward test.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly industrial production index (INDPRO) exceeding 93.6 (2017=100) during a period of declining inflation (CPIAUCSL < 225) signals resilient manufacturing momentum that supports S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: Across 50 such supply-up months with low inflation, the 20-day forward return mean is not significantly above zero (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the 1-month change in FEDFUNDS crosses above 0.5%, it indicates a shift toward tighter policy, which raises the cost of capital and dampens equity valuation growth, producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS increases by >0.5% in a month
failure_condition: In >70% of prior tightening months, the 20-day forward return was non-negative, or the 20-day discount premium remains positive.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the unemployment rate below 4% for three consecutive months is accompanied by rising labor force participation, which boosts consumer spending and supports positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE falls below 4% for three consecutive months
failure_condition: During such labor regimes, 60-day forward returns are not statistically higher than during prior shallow-labor periods (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sudden drop in retail sales (not directly observable in the provided catalog but proxy via PAYEMS decline) followed by a rebound exceeding 2% in the next month suggests cyclical bottoming, which often precedes equity market optimism and drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS falls for two months then rises by >2% in the third month
failure_condition: In 40% of such rebounds, the 5-day forward return does not exceed the pre-rebound 5-day average (p > 0.1).

mechanism_narrative: When the ratio of industrial production (INDPRO) to GDP growth (from GDP series not in catalog but implied via INDPRO context) accelerates above 1.5% in a month, it indicates stronger output momentum that correlates with higher investor confidence and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO growth rate > 1.5% in a month
failure_condition: During 30 such months, the 20-day forward return mean is not significantly positive (p > 0.05).
